narrative.headline: Top 50 tilts decisively bullish — 30 of 50 names lean long with heavy near-money call premium and supportive dark pool prints, while a handful of mega-caps including AAPL, META, GOOG show structural distribution.
bullish_setups: ABBV: perfect 10.0 composite — flow, dark pool ($293M), and blocks all max conviction
TXN: 10.0 across the board with $1.29M flow premium and $337M dark pool
GE: $9M flow premium + $762M dark pool — heavy industrial accumulation
AVGO: $119M flow premium (largest in scan) + $970M dark pool — semis being aggressively bid
AMZN: $18.5M flow premium + $778M dark pool, blocks maxed
AMAT + KLAC: semi-cap equipment showing coordinated call buying + 9.6-10.0 dark pool conviction
HD/WMT/PEP: defensive consumer staples/discretionary all flow 10.0 — barbell with semis
WFC: flow 8.59 backed by $439M dark pool and max blocks — bank accumulation outlier
bearish_setups: AAPL: flow 3.36 — put-side dominant despite max dark pool/blocks (distribution into liquidity)
META: flow 3.00 with 10.0 dark pool/blocks — classic structural distribution pattern
GOOG: flow 1.69 — weakest mega-cap tech flow, heavy block selling
KO: flow 1.37 — defensive name being unwound, contrasts with PEP/WMT bid
V: flow 2.65 + max dark pool/blocks — distribution while MA shows opposite (flow 10.0)
UNH: flow 3.53, healthcare laggard vs ABBV strength
GS/MS/AXP: financials ex-WFC showing put-side flow despite high dark pool magnitude
narrative.rotation_signal: Clear rotation INTO semis (AVGO, AMAT, KLAC, TXN), industrials (GE, GEV, CAT), and select consumer (HD, WMT, PEP, ABBV) — and OUT OF mega-cap tech platforms (AAPL, META, GOOG) and payment networks (V). Pair trades stand out: MA bullish vs V bearish, PEP bullish vs KO bearish, WFC bullish vs GS/MS bearish — institutions are picking winners within sectors rather than buying the sector.
narrative.diverging_from_industry_layer: AAPL, META, GOOG bearish read may diverge from broader tech-positive industry narratives — Top 50 sees distribution where index-level tech looks strong. Financials split: WFC bullish vs GS/MS/AXP bearish suggests the bank trade is name-specific, not sector-wide.
